items.title: Source site contradicts itself on scope and size
items.summary: The source page header says "Pass C · 17 Aug 2026", its dataset says pass S / reviewed 2026-08-19, and its own review.html says the ledger "now runs to 119 listings" while the data holds 206. The numbers on the source homepage (206 / 189 / 62 / 60) are computed by its JavaScript, not written into the data.
evidence: index.html of the source site: subtitle "Pass C · 17 Aug 2026".
assets/data.js header: "pass S, 2026-08-19", reviewed: "2026-08-19".
review.html of the source site: "the ledger now runs to 119 listings".
items.action: We publish the dataset's own numbers and state the pass and date we used. No figure on our site is taken from the source page's marketing header.

items.title: Every prize figure is 74 days stale at publication
items.summary: All 206 rows carry "last checked 2026-08-19". Today is 2026-11-01 — a 74-day gap. Contest prize tables, seasons and eligibility change on that timescale, and several sports contests in the set are seasonal.
evidence: Ledger field lastChecked = "2026-08-19" on all 206 rows.
Source repository last commit 2026-08-19T22:07:51Z.
items.action: Shown on every page as "source reviewed 2026-08-19". Prize figures are labelled as the source's claims, and each row links to the operator so the live figure can be read before entering.

items.title: Ended / out-of-season contests are still listed with prize figures
items.summary: 27 listings are marked "ended / out of season" by the source itself yet still carry a prize figure. They must not be presented as things to enter today.
evidence: Rows with status "ended" (e.g. espn-pigskin, fox-super6, nba-pickem, yahoo-bracket-mayhem).
items.action: Separated on the site: excluded from every shortlist and from the "enter now" count; shown with an "Ended" stamp in the full table and on its category page.

items.title: No official-source link on the row — prize figure has no official basis
items.summary: 11 listings cite only affiliate or forum sources. Three of them say so in their own text: the prize table was taken from review sites, not the operator.
evidence: Rows whose sources array contains no entry with tier "official".
roboforex-demo restricted field: "Prize table sourced from review sites, not the official domain — re-confirm before relying on it."
fbs-pro-demo and npbfx-demo carry the same note.
items.action: The prize cell is left BLANK for these rows on the site, marked "unverified", and the row is listed here. The dataset's own wording is shown in the row detail, clearly labelled as an unconfirmed claim.

items.title: Official iOS link returns an error page
items.summary: The App Store link for Solitaire Cash (id1252281551) returned Apple's "An Error Occurred" page on 2026-11-01, while a different apps.apple.com link fetched in the same session loaded normally. The app is likely no longer on the US storefront, but one observation is not proof.
evidence: Fetch of https://apps.apple.com/us/app/solitaire-cash-win-real-money/id1252281551 returned title "App Store", body "An Error Occurred".
Control fetch of https://apps.apple.com/us/app/skillz-arena/id6761981587 rendered a full app page.
items.action: Row keeps the operator link and shows the App Store link marked "reported error 2026-11-01". Human confirmation needed.

items.title: Rules link points at a past, finished contest
items.summary: The TradingView row links its "rules" to the named July 2026 event, and on 2026-11-01 the programme's landing page showed every event as completed. The generic entry point is the useful link, not a single expired event's rules.
evidence: rulesUrl: https://www.tradingview.com/the-leap/tradestation-july-2026/rules/
Landing page on 2026-11-01 listed events through "October 7 – 20, 2026", marked Completed.

links.title: Expired rules link cited by the source

items.action: Row leads with the programme page; the expired rules link is shown as "past contest rules" rather than presented as current terms.

items.title: Referral / promo codes published with no verification
items.summary: 12 rows carry a referral or league code. Eight are explicitly marked codeVerified: false and four have no verification flag at all. Referral codes are personal or affiliate incentives, they change without notice, and a code can never be confirmed as "the operator's official offer".
evidence: Rows with a "code" field, e.g. ffs-fpl (eikrq4), fplhub (00ul99), olka (5nysyw), pitchbooking (5hwilh).
codeVerified is false on 8 of the 12 and unspecified on the other 4.
items.action: Codes are NOT published on this site. The row is shown without a code and this entry explains why. If you want them, take them from the operator page, not from this ledger.

items.title: No rules URL at all
items.summary: 6 rows have no rules/terms URL, so a reader cannot check eligibility or prize terms from the row.
evidence: Rows where rulesUrl is null/empty.
items.action: Row shows the operator site only, with a "no rules page cited" note in the detail panel.

items.title: "Rules" link is just the signup page
items.summary: 117 of 206 rows point their rules URL at exactly the same address as the signup URL. The rules are then not a separate, linkable document — the reader lands on a marketing or entry page.
evidence: Rows where rulesUrl === signupUrl.
items.action: Shown as a single "Official page" link instead of pretending there is a separate rules document.

items.title: Insecure (http://) link
items.summary: 1 row links only http://. The host serves the same page over https, so the link should be upgraded.
evidence: squarespool: http://www.squarespool.com/ ; the https version returned the same page on 2026-11-01.
items.action: Our site links the https address. The dataset keeps the original for auditability.

items.title: Gambling-operator and broker-account contests sit inside a ledger that excludes them
items.summary: The source states that sweepstakes, casinos, and "any contest that requires an account with a gambling operator (bookmaker, sportsbook or real-money DFS)" are excluded. 17 rows appear to break that rule: a contest entered through Fanatics' sportsbook/casino product, a contest hosted on a gambling-affiliate domain, and 15 broker demo contests whose own notes call them broker acquisition funnels. Whether they belong in a free-money ledger is your call, not ours — but it should not be silent.
evidence: fanatics-survivor signupUrl is https://betfanatics.com/ — fetched on 2026-11-01: "Fanatics Sports & Casino — Bet $20 Get $350 in FanCash", with Sportsbook and Casino state lists.
dirty-dozen signupUrl is https://www.gambling.com/games/dirty-dozen — a gambling-affiliate domain, contest name "(Gambling.com)".
tickmill-nfp eligibility: "Live Tickmill account holders".
xm-demo / hfm-demo / litefinance-best restricted notes: "Broker acquisition funnel", prizes are trading bonuses or credits.
The source's own category blurb for sports advertises "sweepstakes sportsbooks" while the file header excludes sweepstakes (see I-15).
items.action: These rows are kept (they are free to enter) but are stamped "operator account required" on the site and excluded from the "best free-to-enter" shortlist. Decide whether to drop them.

items.title: Prizes that are points, gems or credits, not dollars
items.summary: The ledger's premise is "free competitions that can pay real money", but a number of rows pay in non-cash currency: Swagbucks SB points, Papaya Gems, Skillz Z coins, broker trading credits. The 2 rows below are the ones where the dataset itself says the free path pays in something other than dollars, or where the payout is a credit rather than cash. Others in the skill category have the same shape without saying so as plainly.
evidence: swagbucks-trivia prize: "SB points redeemable for PayPal cash / gift cards".
givling prize: "Trivia removed — no longer a trivia contest" (the row no longer describes a contest at all).
papaya.com/faq (fetched): free competitions use Gems; cash competitions are separate.
items.action: Each row states its payout currency explicitly ("points", "gems", "account credit"); the shortlist requires a cash-equivalent payout.

items.title: No stated prize amount
items.summary: 143 rows state a money amount; the other 78 do not. They use placeholder text such as "Prizes decided by your group", "Varies", "Confirm in-app" or "Unverified". These rows cannot be ranked on prize value.
evidence: Rows where the prize field contains no currency amount.
items.action: Prize shown as "—" on the site with the reason, and the row is ineligible for the big-prize shortlist.

items.title: Non-USD prize currencies in a USD-framed ledger
items.summary: Some prize figures are in £ or €. They are not converted here — a conversion would be an invented number.
evidence: Rows whose prize text contains £ or € and no $.
items.action: Original currency shown as written; no conversion applied anywhere on the site.

items.title: Directory listings are not themselves free contests
items.summary: The directory rows are catalogues. Fetched on 2026-11-01, Reedsy's writing-contest list showed 458 contests, many of them charging entry fees ($5–$49 observed), and its "prize" is a directory-wide range rather than a prize.
evidence: reedsy-dir prize text: "Listed per contest (hundreds to tens of thousands)".
Fetched page: entry fees $5, $11, $12, $15, $20, $25 and $49 on listed contests.
items.action: Directory rows carry an explicit warning on their detail page, are scored −6 in the shortlist model and never appear in a "best picks" list.

items.title: Category copy tells readers to use sweepstakes sportsbooks, which the same file excludes
items.summary: The sports category blurb in the source data reads: "Daily fantasy freerolls and sweepstakes sportsbooks." The file header says sweepstakes are excluded by policy. Both cannot be true.
evidence: types[sports].blurb: "Daily fantasy freerolls and sweepstakes sportsbooks. Free tickets or free coins can win USD; most large pools are paid-entry."
items.action: We do not repeat that blurb. Our category description is written from what the rows actually contain.

items.title: ESPN's own rules contradict each other on how many entries you may submit
items.summary: Found by the parallel sessions on 2026-11-01: ESPN's FAQ says five entries while the intro and the current picks UI say ten. Both cannot be right, and it changes how a multi-entry strategy works.
evidence: ESPN NFL Pick'em FAQ vs the current picks page, read 2026-11-01 by arena/27a86924-own1 and re-read by arena/90c9f78c-own1 (see research/SOURCES.md).
items.action: The caveat is carried on the row's detail page verbatim as a cross-check note. We do not pick a number.

items.title: Challenge.gov is listed as a live lead, but the government says the platform was sunset on 2026-03-30
items.summary: Found by a parallel session on 2026-11-01: the reference work groups Challenge.gov with other contest platforms, while the government's own site states the platform was sunset in March 2026. A dead directory sends readers to nothing.
evidence: challenge.gov notice read 2026-11-01 (see the archived supplemental research page).
items.action: No Challenge.gov row exists in this ledger, so nothing was removed. Recorded here because the source material presents it as a current directory.

items.title: IceHacks advertises cash in its header but its own description says there are no cash prizes
items.summary: A parallel session found a page contradicting itself: the header advertises cash, the description says no cash prizes. Header copy is not a prize.
evidence: icehacks.devpost.com read 2026-11-01.
items.action: IceHacks is not carried as a row, so no prize is published for it. Recorded so the pattern (headline vs rules) stays visible.

items.title: PayPal AI Hackathon: headline prize total and itemised rules disagree
items.summary: The event page advertises $67,500 cash and $69,750 total prizes; the rules itemise individual awards including non-cash credits. This site quotes only the clearly stated first-place cash award ($12,000) and nothing else.
evidence: Event page vs rules page, read 2026-11-01 by arena/37aed701-own1.
items.action: The row states "$12,000 first place" only, with this discrepancy noted on its detail page. No total is published.

items.title: The blanket claim that "US tax forms apply at $600+" is a generalisation, not a rule
items.summary: A parallel session flagged that the reference work presents a $600 threshold as universal. Reporting depends on the type of income and the filer's circumstances; IRS guidance distinguishes prizes/awards from gambling winnings.
evidence: The source dataset's own verification-level text: "US prizes of $600+ typically require a W-9".
IRS Publication 525 and IRS Topic 419 distinguish other income from gambling winnings.
items.action: Every page that mentions tax says "the source's generalisation" and links this entry. Nothing here is tax advice.

items.title: Metaculus: the slug "us-midterms-2026" returns "Page not found"; the working tournament URL is "midterms-2026"
items.summary: Read 2026-11-02: https://www.metaculus.com/tournament/us-midterms-2026/ returns "Page not found", while https://www.metaculus.com/tournament/midterms-2026/ loads "US Midterms 2026" ($10,000 prize pool, closes Nov 04). The dead slug still appears in the archived Prize Atlas data (data/atlas-entries.json, data/verified.json).
evidence: Both URLs fetched 2026-11-02 by arena/7a477419-own1.
items.action: This site links only the working URL. The archived files were left unchanged and are noted here.

items.title: Meta VR Start Developer Competition: "$1M in cash prizes" but entry is restricted to Meta VR Start members
items.summary: The rules state "NO PURCHASE NECESSARY" and also "THIS CONTEST IS OPEN ONLY TO MEMBERS OF THE META VR START PROGRAM", with a Meta account with Developer Access required. The $1,000,000 figure is the page-title claim; the prize table was not read, so it is shown with that label and the row is marked "some free events", not "free entry".
evidence: Official rules read 2026-11-02 by arena/7a477419-own1.
items.action: Kept as a row with the gate stated. Start membership criteria were not read — check them before planning work.

items.title: Devpost "DSH Hacks V2" title says "$100k+ in prizes!" but the listing shows "5 non-cash prizes"
items.summary: On the Devpost hackathon list read 2026-11-02, the event is titled "DSH Hacks V2 ($100k+ in prizes!)" while the card shows "5 non-cash prizes" (Jun 24 - Nov 15, 2026). A headline in a title is not a cash prize.
evidence: Devpost hackathon listing read 2026-11-02 by arena/7a477419-own1.
items.action: Not carried as a row; recorded so the headline-vs-rules pattern stays visible (see also I-19, I-20).

items.title: Kaggle competition pages state no entry fee but never say "free"
items.summary: For the six Kaggle competitions added on 2026-11-02, neither the overview nor the rules text read contains an entry fee or the word "free", and the Kaggle docs page read does not state it either. Entry is by Kaggle registration and acceptance of the rules. Their entry cell therefore reads "Entry cost not stated" rather than "Free entry".
evidence: Overview pages and the Name That LLM rules page (including the Kaggle foundational rules) read 2026-11-02 by arena/7a477419-own1.

links.title: Name That LLM rules (with foundational rules)

items.action: Left as "not stated". If Kaggle publishes an explicit statement, set freePath to "full" for these rows.

items.title: Two top-ranked entries close today (2026-11-02): ARC Prize competition tracks and Codex x TwitchCon
items.summary: ARC Prize lists "November 2, 2026 - Submissions due" (Kaggle showed "6 hours to go" for ARC-AGI-3 and ARC-AGI-2; the Paper Track is due November 8). Codex x TwitchCon shows "Deadline: Nov 2, 2026 @ 5:00pm EST" and "4 more hours to deadline". Countdowns on this site run from the date of the newest official-page reading.

items.title: Tool-locked or offline-only entries cannot be won with an arbitrary hosted AI agent as the submitted solution
items.summary: ARC Prize: "Internet access is not available during Kaggle evaluation (no API-based systems like GPT/Claude/etc.)". Name That LLM and Enveda CASMI: notebooks with internet disabled. Gemma 4 Developer Agent: the submission must use one allowed Gemma 4 variant. Codex x TwitchCon requires a project built with OpenAI Codex; Kiroween requires Kiro; Codegeist requires Atlassian Forge. An AI coding agent can still help write and test the solution where the rules allow it.
evidence: Official pages read 2026-11-02 by arena/7a477419-own1; quotes are on the Verified shortlist page.
items.action: Stated in the "What the official page says" column of the Verified shortlist. Nothing is scored on it.

items.title: XPRIZE: multi-million purses are shown, but the Quantum Applications page lists selected finalist teams and no entry terms
items.summary: The XPRIZE competitions page lists purses ($5M Quantum Applications, $119M Water Scarcity, $101M Healthspan, $100M Carbon Removal, $10M Rainforest, $11M Wildfire finals). The Quantum Applications page shows 7 finalists and 20 semifinalists chosen by judges; no entry fee, window or eligibility was read, so open entry is not evidenced.
evidence: xprize.org/competitions and /competitions/qc-apps read 2026-11-02 by arena/7a477419-own1.
items.action: The row stays; its entry cell is not asserted as free.

items.title: GEMS Prize: the HeroX page limits entry to U.S.-based entrants, and the closing time differs between pages
items.summary: HeroX (read 2026-11-02): "Institutions, companies, nonprofit organizations, and individuals based in the United States are eligible to compete." It also says submissions are due "December 3 at 5 PM ET", while the DrivenData reading on 2026-11-01 recorded 23:59 UTC the same day. The official rules PDF (nlr.gov) could not be fetched, so the entry fee and full eligibility text were not read. The row is labelled "Entry cost not stated" and the $300,000 pool is the pages' own figure.
evidence: https://www.herox.com/GEMSPrize read 2026-11-02 by arena/7a477419-own1; DrivenData page read 2026-11-01 by arena/27a86924-own1.
items.action: Row kept with the US-based restriction and both closing times in its notes. Read the PDF rules before spending time on it.

items.title: FutureEval Bot Tournament: entry is free, but running a bot costs money and free credits are limited
items.summary: Metaculus' rules say no purchase or fee is required. The resources page also says free AskNews search is for every registered bot maker, donated LLM credits go to "a select number of bot makers who apply", and "We will not be able to cover all AI providers (nor AI costs for especially expensive bots)". Prize split for the $50,000 pool was not read.
evidence: Tournament page, resources page (sections 1-2 of 19) and the Metaculus competition rules read 2026-11-02 by arena/7a477419-own1.
items.action: Stated on the row and on the Verified shortlist. Estimate API cost before committing a bot to the full season.

items.title: Most rows were not re-checked in this pass
items.summary: 13 of 221 rows were fetched live on 2026-11-01. The build sandbox has no general outbound web access, so a 206-row crawl was not possible here. The other 208 rows are published as "source cited — not re-checked this session".
evidence: live-checks.json records 12 fetches; no other URL was retrieved this session.
items.action: Listed openly. Each row carries its own status badge so a reader can tell a live-checked row from a merely cited one.

items.title: Official links that no longer load — their prize figures can no longer be confirmed
items.summary: 37 of 203 external URLs in the row data failed an automated fetch on 2026-11-01. On 2026-11-02 those failures were fetched again by hand by arena/adae2c72-own1: 8 are still dead or erroring (404, DNS not found, 503, expired certificate, or a server error page), and 6 had loaded again (bot walls and transient errors — not flagged). 23 failures were not re-fetched; most are HTTP 403 bot walls that open in a browser. A prize figure whose only official source is one of the dead URLs cannot be confirmed, so 5 prize cell(s) were blanked on that basis and 8 row(s) carry this flag.
evidence: https://bracketchallenge.nhl.com/en/how-to-play — HTTP 404 again on 2026-11-02 (Azure Static Web Apps: "404: Not Found"). Same host as the row's signup URL /en/home, which was not fetched separately.
https://fantasy.football.scot/ — Fetch failed on 2026-11-01 (ENOTFOUND, DNS) and again on 2026-11-02.
https://fantazilig.tff.org/ — Fetch failed on 2026-11-01 (ENOTFOUND, DNS) and again on 2026-11-02.
https://supercoach.news.com.au/bbl/ — Fetch failed on 2026-11-01 (ENOTFOUND, DNS) and again on 2026-11-02.
https://fantasyracing.telegraph.co.uk/cheltenham/how-to-play — Fetch failed on 2026-11-01 (ENOTFOUND, DNS) and again on 2026-11-02.
https://fantasygaelicfootball.com/ — Connection timeout on 2026-11-01 (UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT); fetch failed again on 2026-11-02.
https://dash.hypermind.com/hypermind/app.html — HTTP 503 Service Unavailable on 2026-11-01 and again on 2026-11-02.

https://pensacolabeachsongwritersfestival.com/2026-songwriting-competition/ — TLS certificate expired on 2026-11-01 (CERT_HAS_EXPIRED). On 2026-11-02 the URL loaded but served only a WordPress "There has been a critical error on this website" page - no competition content.
items.action: Affected rows keep their links for auditability but show "—" for the prize and this flag. Re-check the operator by hand before relying on any figure; a DNS failure can be temporary, and the row detail says exactly which URL failed.
